text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Carl Hagen, leader of the Progress Party, wants to form a government with the conservatives, liberal Venstre and the Christian People's Party if they manage to get a majority in the elections in September.
- Ruhrgas head Burckhard Bergmann says the German market has reached saturation point in terms of gas, but says that Norway could sell more gas to Britain and central Europe.
- Because of large amounts of snow in the mountains, experts don't see an increase in electricity prices in the next 12 months.
- Norwegian police are investigating a Norwegian diplomat in a Asian country suspected of selling Norwegian visas.
- According to an analyses by Dagens Naeringsliv shares in Aker Maritime ASA are sold at a correct price of 123 crowns per share.

- Norwegian investments abroad have doubled since 1990, according to statistics from the central bank. Professor Kaare Petter Hagen at the Norwegian school of business and economics says some of the largest Norwegian companies have become too large for the Norwegian market.
